post.summary: Test the connection to a registered camera with its stored credential
post.description:
One read-only connection attempt against the **registered** camera in the path, with the credential the Core holds for it, inside the time limit of operation 95: authenticate, list the media profiles, look for a usable profile, then probe the stream. It changes no setting of the camera and nothing that is stored, and is never repeated without a new operator action.

**Web console only**, as operation 95 (`WEB_CONSOLE_SESSION`): a session of a tablet or a phone is refused `403 NOT_PERMITTED` with `details.reason: WEB_CONSOLE_ONLY` and one ACCESS_DENIED row. Idle only: with a session open it answers `409 CAPTURE_CONFIG_LOCKED` and writes no audit row.

**No body.** No credential, address, host, port, URL, path or profile member exists: the device is the id in the path, the credential is the stored one, and the address is the stored one **under the Core's destination rule for a stored camera** - a stored value is not trusted either. An address the rule refuses answers `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: CANDIDATE_NOT_TESTABLE`, before anything is read or sent.

**The stored credential is read once, for this one test, by the Core itself.** It is never returned, logged, put into an error or kept after the test. The read is audited by its reader: one CAPTURE_CREDENTIAL_REVEALED row (the device, `reason: CONNECTION_TEST`, the operator). The outcome is a second row, CAPTURE_DEVICE_CONNECTION_TESTED: the device id, the outcome, the adapter and its class, the count of usable profiles, and whether the lock-out guard closed - never the username, the secret, an address or a URL.

**A failed test is a `200` result, not an HTTP error**: the five outcomes of operation 95. `authenticated` is always true. The answer holds no device error text, no address and no credential member.

Refusals **before the credential is read** and before any request leaves the Core, with no audit row: `404 NOT_FOUND` for a device that is no registered camera; `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason` `CANDIDATE_NOT_TESTABLE` (a development source, which has no stored credential, or a stored address the Core does not connect to) or `CONNECTION_TEST_IN_PROGRESS`; the bounds below.

**Refusals after the reader of the stored credential was called.** The reader audits every call, so each of these has one CAPTURE_CREDENTIAL_REVEALED row although nothing was sent to the camera: `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` (no credential is stored for this camera - store one with operation 89) and `503 NOT_READY` with `details.reason: CREDENTIAL_STORE_NOT_READY` (the stored credential cannot be read). The outcome row then says `UNREACHABLE` with `unreachableReason: CREDENTIAL_NOT_READ`; a test the adapter refused before a request says `unreachableReason: NOT_SENT`. Without that member an `UNREACHABLE` row means that the camera was asked and did not answer.

Over a bound the Core server answers `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `retry-after` and `details.reason` `CONNECTION_TEST_RATE_LIMITED` or `CONNECTION_TEST_LOCKOUT_GUARD`. **The lock-out guard is the one of operation 95**: refused credentials are counted per camera address, a typed and a stored one together, so a camera whose stored credential was refused is not asked again by this test or by a typed one until the window has passed: nothing is sent and no audit row is written. `503 NOT_READY` carries `details.reason` `DISCOVERY_NOT_READY` when the Core has no production camera adapter or the reader of the stored credential was not provided - **a Core whose capture is simulated, or that runs with development sources, always answers this**, after the idle lock and before the device is looked up, with no audit row - or `CREDENTIAL_STORE_NOT_READY` when the stored credential cannot be read. Both are envelope-level answers of the contract.

Simulated: the in-app simulator emulates this operation (OD-17 supersedes the old "simulator untouched" rule, OD-23); in Simulated mode a client calls it inside its own simulator. The simulator contacts nothing and holds no credential, so nothing can be tested: it answers what a Core server in simulated capture answers, `503 NOT_READY` with `details.reason: DISCOVERY_NOT_READY`, for every id - never a synthetic `REACHABLE`. It writes no audit row and changes no state. With a session open it answers `409 CAPTURE_CONFIG_LOCKED` first; on a tablet or phone it refuses with the same `403`.

post.description:
Records that the installation of this Core was accepted. The body names the steps that were checked and, if there is one, the address of the site. **Everything else is the Core's own fact and cannot be sent**: who accepted (the operator of the session) and when, the software version, a copy of the Core's id, name and room as they are now, and the newest diagnostics run as it is. The answer is the stored record.

**TECHNICIAN only, web console only.** Needs CAPTURE_COMMISSION, which the TECHNICIAN role alone holds, and a web console session (`WEB_CONSOLE_SESSION`): a session of a tablet or a phone is refused `403 NOT_PERMITTED` with `details.reason: WEB_CONSOLE_ONLY` and one ACCESS_DENIED row.

**Idle only.** With a session open it answers `409 CAPTURE_CONFIG_LOCKED` and writes no audit row.

**Recording is not gated on an acceptance.** A session starts whether or not an acceptance is in force, and a revocation stops nothing: the acceptance is a record, not a switch.

**At most one acceptance is in force**, and the database holds that: while one is in force this operation answers `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: INSTALLATION_ACCEPTANCE_IN_FORCE`, also when two requests arrive at the same moment. Revoke it first (operation 110). What was accepted is never rewritten and never removed. When the clock of the Core reads earlier than an instant the installation record already holds (the acceptance in force, or the revocation of an earlier one): `INSTALLATION_CLOCK_BEHIND_RECORD`, nothing is stored and no instant is bent.

**The step list is the contract's, not a screen's.** The steps are the 27 checks of the hardware acceptance package (`9A/H-01` to `9A/H-27`; list version 1), each with a result of the closed set `PASS`, `FAIL`, `NOT_RUN`. The body names EVERY check exactly once: an id outside the list, a missing id, a repeated id and an empty list are refused `422`, and so is a `FAIL` or a `NOT_RUN` without a note that says why. A check that was not run is stated, never left out.

**No free JSON.** A step is exactly `id` (a check of the list), `result` and `detail` (a note on one line, or null); any other member is refused `422`. At most 32 steps; every text at most 200 characters with no line break and no control character; the steps together at most 8192 bytes as the database stores them (one blank after every colon and comma). The size and the one-line rule are refinements a JSON Schema cannot state: the Core applies them. The refusal never quotes the input.

**The diagnostics are read, not sent.** The Core copies its newest diagnostics run. With no run, or a run that has not ended: `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: INSTALLATION_DIAGNOSTICS_NOT_COMPLETE`. A run with a failed check is recorded as it is: the acceptance is the operator's statement, and the record shows what the Core reported. Device text inside the run is made one line and cut to 200 characters before it is stored. A run that still does not fit the record (a value outside the closed key list, or more than 16384 bytes) answers `INSTALLATION_DIAGNOSTICS_NOT_STORABLE`; an id, name, room or version of the Core that does not fit (longer than its bound, or not on one line) answers `INSTALLATION_SITE_NOT_STORABLE`. Nothing is stored in either case.

On success writes one INSTALLATION_ACCEPTED row whose details are `acceptanceId`, `stepCount` and `passedCount` (the checks whose result is `PASS`): the record id and counts only, never a step, a site text or the diagnostics.

Simulated: the in-app simulator emulates this operation (OD-17 supersedes the old "simulator untouched" rule, OD-23); in Simulated mode a client calls it inside its own simulator. The simulator keeps no installation record: a body of the right form answers `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: INSTALLATION_ACCEPTANCE_NOT_AVAILABLE`. It stores nothing, writes no audit row and changes no state.

**Recording is not gated on an acceptance.** A session starts whether or not an acceptance is in force, and a revocation stops nothing: the acceptance is a record, not a switch.

The simulator never holds an acceptance: a body of the right form answers `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: INSTALLATION_ACCEPTANCE_NOT_IN_FORCE`. post.summary: Retire a registered camera or microphone
post.description:
**Retires ONE registered camera or microphone for good.** Its stored credential is **destroyed** in the same unit of work; its registry row is **kept** with `retiredAt` and `retiredBy` set, together with its stream rows and its audio input row, so every sealed package and every audit row that names its id keeps its meaning. A retired device is **never assigned again**, never tested (operation 108), never given a credential (89) or an address (100), and it is no longer "registered" for an adoption: **adopting the same unit again (operations 95/96, or 99 for a microphone) gives a NEW id** - an id is never reused. There is no way back and no hard delete.

**TECHNICIAN only, web console only.** Needs CAPTURE_COMMISSION, which the TECHNICIAN role alone holds, and a web console session (`WEB_CONSOLE_SESSION`): a session of a tablet or a phone is refused `403 NOT_PERMITTED` with `details.reason: WEB_CONSOLE_ONLY` and one ACCESS_DENIED row.

**Idle only.** With a session open it answers `409 CAPTURE_CONFIG_LOCKED` and writes no audit row.

**The body is the reason only**: `REMOVED`, `REPLACED` or `STATEMENT_CHANGED` - a closed set, so no free text reaches the audit row. No credential, address or profile member exists.

Refusals, each storing nothing and writing no audit row, in this order after the role, the web console and the idle lock: `422 INVALID_INPUT` for a body of another form; `404 NOT_FOUND` for an id the registry does not hold; `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason` `CAPTURE_DEVICE_BUILT_IN` (a built-in device of the demonstration model - `CAM-01`, `CAM-02`, `CAM-03`, `CAM-04`, `MIC-01`, `MIC-02`, `MIC-03`, `MIC-04`, `POE-SWITCH` - or any PoE switch), `CAPTURE_DEVICE_RETIRED` (retired already), `CAPTURE_DEVICE_ASSIGNED` (a slot of the device selector names it; `details.slot` names the slot: unassign it first) or `CONNECTION_TEST_IN_PROGRESS` (operation 108 is testing this camera).

**On success writes one CAPTURE_DEVICE_RETIRED row** (category SECURITY): `deviceId`, `kind` (CAMERA or MIC), `reason`, `credentialDestroyed`, `streamRowsKept` (a count), `operationId` and `permission` - never an address, a hardware id, a serial or a credential. The answer is the device entry after the change. The `captureDevices` slice keeps the entry with `retiredAt` set: a client lists it as Retired and leaves it out of every selector and assignment list.

Simulated: the in-app simulator emulates this operation (OD-17 supersedes the old "simulator untouched" rule, OD-23); in Simulated mode a client calls it inside its own simulator. The simulator holds no credential: it retires a device it registered itself (an adopted camera) in its own state and writes the same CAPTURE_DEVICE_RETIRED row with `credentialDestroyed: false` and `streamRowsKept: 0`; its built-in devices answer `CAPTURE_DEVICE_BUILT_IN`. Same order of refusals as the Core server's.

post.description:
Returns a short-lived URL of the registry-external route `GET /preview/{token}`, which streams the camera in the path as motion JPEG (`multipart/x-mixed-replace`, about 8 pictures per second at 640x360; `Cache-Control: no-store`). The token (prefix `cps_`) is a random bearer value bound to the operator, the sign-in session and the camera; it must be opened within 60 s and never enters a log or an audit row. A stream that is open is cut when its sign-in session ends (checked every 10 s).

Needs SESSION_START, CAPTURE_CONFIG or DEVICE_MANAGE (decision D53: everyone who can start a session). The route `GET /preview/{token}` has the same rule. The camera must be a registered production camera: the Core reads its stored credential for the preview (one CAPTURE_CREDENTIAL_REVEALED row, `reason: PREVIEW_OPEN`, when the stream is started), never returns it.

**Recording always has priority.** A preview yields its camera before a pre-check and before a session opens it, and resumes after the recording's push stands, while viewers remain. Bounds: 1 stream per camera, 4 in all, 4 viewers per camera and 16 in all; over a bound the Core answers `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `details.reason: PREVIEW_LIMIT` (an envelope-level answer) and writes no row. A Core without a live preview answers `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: PREVIEW_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

Writes CAMERA_PREVIEW_OPENED before the answer: the device, `expiresAt` and the operation - never the token or the URL.

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

get.description:
The firmware version the LCD front panel reported **about itself**, plus the panel link word of the panel backend. Distinct from `GET /api/v1/device/health`, which is the Core state and needs a signed-in operator.

**Public: it answers a caller with no session.** The screen that shows it is the sign-in screen, which has no credential yet. It is the third public read, beside `getServiceHealth` and `getSignInStatus`.

**What the answer holds, and nothing else:** two short strings — the version the panel stated in a line of its own over USB, and the backend's word for the panel link. No evidence data, no session data, no operator, no channel list, no serial, port or path. This extends the disclosure `GET /api/v1/health` already makes of the service name and version by one string; the extension is small and is taken on purpose, because the alternative is a sign-in screen that cannot say which front panel is attached.

**An absent panel is a `200`, never a failure.** No bridge configured, no backend listening, a backend slower than one second, or a body that is not what the backend's schema says: all four answer `200` with both strings empty, so the sign-in screen keeps working while the front panel is not plugged in. The Core asks the backend at most once per five seconds and gives the call one second, so a polling screen cannot flood it.

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

The two built-in cameras of the demonstration model keep the model's `LIVE` / `LOST` from the registry flag, as their registry entries do (finding JW-23: that is no reading of a stream).

online.description: On a Core in its own capture this is the registry flag of the device (`capture_devices.enabled`), NOT a reachability reading: it is true from the moment the device is registered and changes only when a pre-check, a session start or a microphone re-scan has actually asked the source (false: it did not answer; true again: it answered). Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

items.description: One microphone slot of the device selector.

revision.description: Selector revision the snapshot was taken at.

audioSource.description: The transcription pair of this session: the inputs of channels `MIC-01` and `MIC-02` (D61, 2026-11-04: all four channels record; op 81 moves the transcribed one).

switchedAt.description: When the last switch took effect; null before the first.

intervalFromMs.description: Media-pts start of the interval the switch opened (never wall clock).

captureDurable.description: False from the accepted start until the first durable fragment ("connecting cameras"), then true; the state stays RECORDING (D84, D91 R-1). Absent reads as true.

finalization.description: Finalization v2 of this session; absent before sealing starts.

progress.description: Sealing progress of this step, 0..100 (E-13: Core instants only).

attempt.description: Attempt of this step, >= 1; a resumed run increments it (OD-08).

online.description: On a Core in its own capture this is the registry flag of the device (`capture_devices.enabled`), NOT a reachability reading: it is true from the moment the device is registered and changes only when a pre-check, a session start or a microphone re-scan has actually asked the source (false: it did not answer; true again: it answered). Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

streamState.description: A lost stream is what makes a PoE cycle legal (OD-22). NULL = NOT READ (task 4 row V7c; decision C126 (b)): the Core reads no stream of this camera now, so it states neither LIVE nor LOST - the value of a registered camera at rest, the same as its registry entry's. `LIVE` is stated only while the capture ingest of an open session receives the stream (telemetry `CONNECTED`) - a pre-check or re-scan that reached the camera read its control service, not its stream, and states NULL (row V7d); `LOST` while a stream fault of the camera is active or the ingest waits or ended under a recording; the ingest closing after the stop gives NULL again. The two built-in cameras of the demonstration model keep the model's `LIVE` / `LOST` from the registry flag, as their registry entries do (finding JW-23: that is no reading of a stream).

adapter.description: The adapter kind behind the device (C3 §2.6 "Device shapes"): `ONVIF_RTSP`, `USB_AUDIO`, `SNMP_POE`, `FAKE` or `LOCAL_DEVICE`. Present on a device that operation 96 registered.

sourceClass.description: Derived by the Core from `adapter`: `DEVELOPMENT` exactly for `FAKE` and `LOCAL_DEVICE`. Never set by a client.

sourceOpen.description: True while the Core holds this source open (C3 §2.6, erratum PE-128-38; SEC35-44 (4)): the "is on" fact of a `LOCAL_DEVICE` - the short open of a pre-check included. A runtime fact, never stored: absent when the source is not open, after a restart until it opens, and always in simulated capture.

profiles.description: The stream profiles the Core holds stored for this camera (`capture_devices.profiles`), in the stored order, each code once. A production camera is assigned to a track with ONE of them: the `code` is sent as `profile` of a camera line of operation 78 (operation 79 carries no profile). An EMPTY list: the Core holds no profile for this camera - it cannot be assigned, and no default stands in (C36). Present on every registered camera (one that operation 96 added); absent on every other entry (a microphone, the PoE switch, a built-in device). No credential, no address, no URL, no text of the camera.

code.description: The profile code (`HEVC_1080P`, `H264_720P30`): upper-case letters, digits and underscores, 1 to 64 characters. The value a camera line of operation 78 names as `profile`.

codec.description: The codec the code states: a closed set. Null when the code is no stream statement. Never a default.

resolution.description: The picture the code states: `<height>p` for a 16:9 picture, else `<width>x<height>`. Null when the code is no stream statement. Never a default.

fps.description: The whole-number rate the code states, 1 to 240; null when it states none (an HEVC stream states no rate). Never a default.

items.description: One stored stream profile of a camera: its code and what the code states of the stream.

retiredAt.description: When the device was retired (operation 111, `capture_devices.retired_at`). PRESENT ONLY ON A RETIRED DEVICE, always together with `retiredBy`: its stored credential is destroyed, it is never assigned again, and a client lists it with a Retired state and leaves it out of every selector and assignment list. Absent: the device is in service. A retired device stays in the registry for good (its id is never reused).

retiredBy.description: The operator who retired the device (`OPR-NNN`). Present exactly when `retiredAt` is.

items.description: One capture device (`dbc-3 §B.2`); carries no credential (RK-12).

dbfs.description: Ballistic level in dBFS; -90 means no signal.

noSignal.description: An input that should deliver samples delivers none (a fault word). Never set for a level that is simply not measured: see `notMeasured`.

notMeasured.description: Present and true when the Core does not measure this input now: no capture is open on a Core in its own capture. `dbfs` / `peak` then hold the floor as placeholders and `noSignal` is false; a client draws "Not measured" - no bars, no number, no "NO SIGNAL". Absent: the frame is a measured (or, on a simulated Core, generated) level.

additionalProperties.description: One 20 Hz audio frame: numbers and booleans only.

inputs.description: The newest frame of each mic input of the capture, keyed by input ID `MIC-NN`: a built-in `MIC-01`..`MIC-04`, or another microphone the selector holds (D133 (1) widened by D61, 2026-11-04). One frame per microphone line of the selector, so at most four; fewer while a microphone channel is not assigned.

activeInputId.description: The input whose level is the one inside AUDIO-01 right now (op 81 moves it). Null: the selector holds no PRIMARY microphone.

AudioSlice.description: Slice `audio`: the newest frame of each mic input plus the active one. Streamed in `meters` messages only; not part of a snapshot.

ReplicatedState.description: The 30 replicated slices of the Core state. No `auth`, `authLockout`, `pairing`, `clock` or `audio`, and no other member.

input.description: The create input after normalisation; `notes` is empty when none was given.

value.description: Live device state, e.g. ONLINE, READY, NO_SIGNAL, GNSS.

reason.description: Why the check warns or blocks (English fallback).

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable reason; null while pending or on PASS.

params.description: Values for the reason copy, e.g. `{ track: "AUDIO-01" }`.

sendingDeviceId.description: The paired device that sent this pre-check (fix wave I, D216): the audit row of its outcome names it. Absent: a web console session sent it.

etaMs.description: Estimated milliseconds left for this step.

detail.description: What the progress line shows (fragment count, chunk counters).

attempt.description: Attempt of this step, >= 1; a resumed run increments it.

label.description: English fallback; a client renders its own copy from `kind` and `params`.

coreNotRunning.description: Present on the restart fault of a Core in its own capture: the Core was not running while the session was active and does not know why. The kind stays `POWER_FAIL`; the fault is worded from this member, never as a power failure (closing pass J, D217 (5)). Absent: the fault is what its kind says.

fault.description: The critical fault that moved the session to FAULT, if any.

startTimeSource.description: Time source when the recording started.

stopTimeSource.description: Time source when the recording stopped or faulted.

captureConfig.description: Capture-config snapshot of this session (SH-06 writes it at start).

deviceId.description: The capture device feeding this track (`CAM-01`/`CAM-02`).

profile.description: Media profile code; an open set (OD-05/OD-06).

online.description: On a Core in its own capture this is the registry flag of the device (`capture_devices.enabled`), NOT a reachability reading: it is true from the moment the device is registered and changes only when a pre-check, a session start or a microphone re-scan has actually asked the source (false: it did not answer; true again: it answered). Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

streamState.description: A lost stream is what makes a PoE cycle legal (OD-22). NULL = NOT READ (task 4 row V7c; decision C126 (b)): the Core reads no stream of this camera now, so it states neither LIVE nor LOST - the value of a registered camera at rest, the same as its registry entry's. `LIVE` is stated only while the capture ingest of an open session receives the stream (telemetry `CONNECTED`) - a pre-check or re-scan that reached the camera read its control service, not its stream, and states NULL (row V7d); `LOST` while a stream fault of the camera is active or the ingest waits or ended under a recording; the ingest closing after the stop gives NULL again. The two built-in cameras of the demonstration model keep the model's `LIVE` / `LOST` from the registry flag, as their registry entries do (finding JW-23: that is no reading of a stream).

items.description: One video slot of the device selector.

channel.description: The selector channel this row fills (D61): `MIC-01`..`MIC-04`; channel 1 feeds the transcribed track `AUDIO-01`.

inputId.description: The mic input, `MIC-NN`: a built-in `MIC-01`..`MIC-04`, or a microphone registered later (D115 (2)).

deviceId.description: The microphone behind the input: the device of the same ID (D106 (4)).

online.description: On a Core in its own capture this is the registry flag of the device (`capture_devices.enabled`), NOT a reachability reading: it is true from the moment the device is registered and changes only when a pre-check, a session start or a microphone re-scan has actually asked the source (false: it did not answer; true again: it answered). Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

items.description: One microphone slot of the device selector.

revision.description: Selector revision the snapshot was taken at.

audioSource.description: The active/standby mic pair of this session.

switchedAt.description: When the last switch took effect; null before the first.

intervalFromMs.description: Media-pts start of the interval the switch opened (never wall clock).

captureDurable.description: False from the accepted start until the first durable fragment ("connecting cameras"), then true; the state stays RECORDING (D84, D91 R-1). Absent reads as true.

captureCheckpoints.description: What the Core holds of a recording of its OWN capture: the fragment checkpoints the capture worker reported durable. Not stored; refreshed at most every 5 s and at the end of the capture. Absent in simulated capture, before the first checkpoint and on a session read back after a restart: absent means "not stated", never 0 (wave H Z1).

fragments.description: Durable fragment checkpoints of all camera files.

bytes.description: Stored bytes of the camera files the checkpoints cover (plaintext on the evidence volume until the seal).

lastAt.description: The Core clock at the newest checkpoint.

transcript.description: Transcript progress of the open session.

sha256.description: Null until the transcript is assembled and hashed.

ActiveSession.description: The open session with its pre-check, timeline, notes and finalization.

origin.description: Present on the one note of an EVIDENCE ITEM that carries the text of the session form's "Notes" field (`id: NOTE-FORM`, `at` = the creation of the session, `authorId` = who created it): written before the recording, copied onto the item when the item was made. Absent on a note written during the recording, and on every note of an open session.

SessionNote.description: A note an investigator wrote during the recording - or, on an evidence item, the session form's note (`origin`).

faultKind.description: INCOMPLETE only: the fault that ended it.

unsealableCause.description: Operation 38 only, on an INCOMPLETE entry that recorded and has no evidence item (its recordings are in the quarantine folder): the cause the Core recorded when it gave the seal up, as a code - `details.cause` of the audit row `SESSION_INCOMPLETE` (`details.reason: UNSEALABLE`) of that session, e.g. `SIGNING_KEY_UNAVAILABLE`. An open set. Read from the audit trail at each call, never reconstructed; absent when the trail holds no such row, on every other entry, and in the replicated `sessionHistory` slice (there the active alert of the session carries the same code: `params.cause` of the alert whose `target` is the session and whose `params.reason` is `UNSEALABLE`).

tracks.description: VIDEO-01, VIDEO-02, AUDIO-01 and AUDIO-02, each with its own hash. The two audio tracks are never merged.

value.description: sha256(manifestHash and keyId) for the simulated stand-in; the Ed25519 signature of the manifest hash for a real one.

algorithm.description: Schema v2: real seals sign with Ed25519 (OD-02); the stand-in remains for v1 rows.

developmentKey.description: Core server only: whether the certificate the SEALED manifest names is a development key - true / false as read from the item's own sealed manifest and certificate; null: could not be established (the package or its certificate is not readable). Absent: not stated (Simulated mode, a v1 item) - never to be read as a production key.

signature.description: The signature of the manifest: the simulated stand-in (v1) or a real Ed25519 (schema v2).

tampered.description: Set by the evidence tamper demo fault; verification then fails.

files.description: Schema v2: one whole file per camera (D224/D225) with its hashes; mirrors the simulator's `EvidenceFileEntry` (SH-07).

trackId.description: The track the file carries (VIDEO-01, VIDEO-02, AUDIO-01).

fileName.description: Relative path inside the package; never absolute or credential-bearing.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the whole file's stored bytes.

fragmentCount.description: Fragments the append-only file was written in (0 for the synthetic legacy shape).

sha256Plain.description: SHA-256 of the plaintext bytes (stored-bytes vs plaintext: both hashes verify).

fragmentChainHead.description: Head of this file's per-fragment hash chain (`dbc-3 §B.12`).

profile.description: Core server only, with `sealedPackage: PRESENT`: the SIGNED manifest's `tracks[].profile` of this file (manifest field 36), e.g. `H264_720P30` - the format the recorded stream declares, not the session's `profileId`. Absent: not stated (no sealed manifest was read).

fragmentChainHead.description: Schema v2 item-level chain head (SH-07 preview shape): the chain the fragments of this item continue.

transcriptSha256.description: Schema v2 item-level transcript hash (SH-07 preview; `evidence_items.transcript_sha256`, dbc-3 §B.11).

manifestVersion.description: Manifest version of the seal (`evidence_items.manifest_version`, dbc-3 §B.11): 2 for every v2 seal, also one without a transcript hash. Absent: derived as before.

labelsStatus.description: Whether the sealed transcript carries speaker labels (`evidence_items.labels_status`); null or absent when the seal states none.

developmentSources.description: Whether the seal recorded a development source (`evidence_items.development_sources`, manifest field 126; C3 §3.1 erratum PE-128-32). Null or absent: not recorded (a v1 item, or one sealed before the column existed) - never to be read as production.

audioSourceIntervals.description: Schema v2: which mic input fed AUDIO-01 over which media-pts spans (op 82 serves the full rows). On a Core, for a sealed item: the intervals of the SEALED manifest (`audio.sourceIntervals`, `seq` from 1), read from the item's own package.

toMs.description: Media-pts end; null for the open interval of a live session.

sourceClass.description: Wave H C1: the source class of the microphone of this interval as the sealed manifest records it (field 125). Absent: not stated.

sealedPackage.description: Core server only, for an item whose sealed v2 package lies in the Core's own store by its facts (a product seal, a seed-sealed demo item). PRESENT: its manifest was read from the package under the digest of record, and `files`, `audioSourceIntervals`, `interrupted` and `signature.developmentKey` are that manifest's. NOT_READABLE: the package is gone or its manifest is not the one the item was sealed with - no sealed fact is stated. Absent: the item has no package in the Core's store (a v1 demo item, a simulated item) - a client then shows nothing of a Core package.

interrupted.description: Core server only: the sealed manifest's `timeline.interrupted` - the package is the sealed durable prefix of a recording that did not end by a stop. Absent: not stated (no sealed manifest was read).

interruptedCause.description: Core server only, with `interrupted: true`: the code the item's custody entry `RECORDING_INTERRUPTED` names (a fault kind), or null when it names none.

streamProfileNotice.description: Core server only, operation 40: the session of this item carries the notice `STREAM_PROFILE_DIFFERS` (an alert of kind SYSTEM with that `params.reason`) - the recorded stream of the named tracks was not the configured profile, and the manifest states the stream. Present while the Core's alert list holds that notice. ABSENT: the Core holds no such notice for the session - never to be read as "compared and equal" for an item older than the alert list.

stream.description: What the recorded stream declared: the value the manifest states.

configured.description: What the selector had configured for the track.

transcriptModel.description: Core server only, for an item whose sealed v2 package lies in the Core's own store and whose SIGNED manifest declares a transcript document: the model of that transcript, from the manifest (decision D160). The same shape as `transcriptModel` of operation 41. For a server backend only the name exists, as reported by the STT server; version, quantisation and file hash are null and were not verified by the Core. Absent: not stated (no document sealed, a v1 or demonstration item, a package that could not be read, a manifest whose signature did not hold) - a reader draws nothing.

name.description: The model name the sealed manifest records.

version.description: The version the installation declared; null for a server backend.

quantisation.description: The quantisation read from the model file; null for a server backend.

modelSha256.description: SHA-256 of the model file as the Core hashed it; null for a server backend.

reportedByServer.description: True when the session's STT backend was a server: the name is what the server reported, and the Core verified nothing of the model.

report.description: The report line of the model, as operation 41 words it.

transcript.description: Schema v2: the transcript summary inside the item; the body arrives through op 84.

state.description: DISABLED only when R-8 turns STT off (D20; lands with M6).

sha256.description: Hash of the canonical transcript document; null until assembled.

machineTranscriptHash.description: Hash of the SEALED machine transcript — byte-unchanged by any revision (OD-15).

revision.description: Current max(revision_no); 0 when no revision exists (SEC35-21).

failedChunks.description: Chunks (not attempts) that ended FAILED; above 0 only with state PARTIAL. No text stands in for a failed chunk (D-EV-1; manifest field 93).

backendUnreachable.description: True when STT was enabled but the configured backend could not be reached for one or more chunks (manifest field 122).

EvidenceItem.description: One evidence item (schema v2 adds files, audio-source intervals and the transcript summary).

message.description: English fallback; a client renders its own copy from `type` and `params`.

SimEvent.description: One operational event. It never holds a password, a token, a code or a credential (SR-54).

kind.description: A fault kind, or SYSTEM for an alert no fault raised.

target.description: The fault target key, so clearing one target resolves its alert.

actorId.description: Operator ID, or null for the system. Never a username typed at a failed sign-in.

message.description: English fallback; a client renders its own copy from `type` and `details`.

deviceId.description: A device of the Core (e.g. CAM-01) or a paired device of the registry (`DEV-NNNN`), or null.

details.description: Flat values. Never a password, a token, a code, a credential or a typed username (SR-54).

hash.description: sha256(prevHash and the canonical JSON of the twelve members above).

AuditRow.description: One audit row with its full hashed body, so a client can verify the chain itself.

connectionId.description: Names this socket in the server's log. Not a credential.

epoch.description: The epoch of the Core state when the connection opened.

principal.description: Who the server took this connection for, from the upgrade request's headers only.

reason.description: Only with ANONYMOUS: the connection presented a credential the server did not accept.

topics.description: The topics this connection is given. Always `heartbeat`; never more than the principal's set.

serverTime.description: Epoch milliseconds on the server clock.

RealtimeHello.description: First message of every connection: who the server took the caller for, and what it will send.

RealtimeSnapshot.description: The whole replicated state: after `hello`, as the answer to `resync`, and when a new epoch starts.

head.description: Hash of the newest row after the append.

total.description: Rows ever appended, after the append.

dropped.description: Rows dropped off the front of the ring, after the append.

RealtimeDeltaOp.description: One operation of a delta: `replace` one whole slice, or `append` rows to `audit` or `events`.

revision.description: Exactly the previous revision plus 1 within the epoch. Revisions are gap-free.

ops.description: Applied in order. A slice no op names is not touched.

RealtimeDelta.description: One change of the replicated state. State deltas are never dropped.

seq.description: Counts the frames the server produced; a skipped frame leaves a gap, by design. It never goes back on a connection, also across a new epoch.

RealtimeMeters.description: One meter frame of both mic inputs, with the active one (SH-17). Sent only after `subscribe`; it carries no revision, and the latest value wins.

operator.description: The operator of the session: ID and new role, nothing else.

permissions.description: The permissions of the new role. A display hint: the server decides every call.

RealtimeSessionUpdated.description: The role of the session's operator changed. The session stays; nobody is signed out.

RealtimeSessionEnded.description: The session of this socket ended. The server closes the connection with 4401 right after.

RealtimeDeviceRevoked.description: The device of this socket is no longer paired. The server closes the connection with 4403 right after.

RealtimeAdminChanged.description: A list of an administration page changed. It names the list only; the client refetches it through REST.

oneOf.description: Start the `meters` frames on this connection.
Stop the `meters` frames on this connection.
Ask for a new `snapshot` after a revision gap or another epoch. At most one in 2 s; one that comes sooner is answered when the 2 s have passed.

RealtimeClientMessage.description: A message a client sends on `/ws`. Anything else closes the connection with 1008; a message larger than 65,536 bytes closes it with 1009.

label.description: Label of the marker: at most 80 UTF-16 code units after trimming. Omitted or empty: the Core names it "Marker n".

text.description: The note: 1 to 2,000 characters after trimming, and at most 2,000 UTF-16 code units. It stays in the session record; the audit row holds its ID and length only.

caseNumber.description: The next case number `LP/{YYYY}/{MMDD}-NNNN`. It is reserved: the next scan offers another.

CaseNumberScan.description: Result of the simulated case-number scanner.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

PageQuery.description: Query of a list read that takes no filter: the paging members of API-9.

items.description: Finished sessions, newest first: the elements of the `sessionHistory` slice.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

SessionHistoryPage.description: One page of the session history.

caseType.description: Only items of this case type (the subject type of the session).

q.description: Search text, 1 to 100 characters after trimming: matched without regard to case against the evidence ID, the session ID, the case number and the subject name.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

EvidenceListQuery.description: Query of `GET /api/v1/evidence`: filters, a search text and the paging members of API-9.

items.description: Evidence items, newest recording first: the elements of the `evidence` slice.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

source.description: DEMO_PACKAGE: the demo package a client bundles belongs to this item. LIVE_STREAM (schema v2): a signed media session (op 88) can play the decrypted camera file. NONE: no media exists for it.

packageSuffix.description: The join key of the bundled package, e.g. `0004`; null when the source is not DEMO_PACKAGE.

fileIds.description: Core server only, with LIVE_STREAM: the camera files the sealed package of the item really holds (one to four, D60 - a package sealed before the widening holds its own two), in file order - the `fileId` values operation 88 accepts for it.

reason.description: Core server only, with NONE: why no media can be played, as a code. `NOT_SEALED` (the item was never sealed: an interrupted or unsealable recording), `NOT_A_SEALED_PACKAGE` (no sealed package of this item lies in the Core's store and no bundled demo package belongs to it), `DEMONSTRATION_RECORD` (fix wave J: the item is the record of a session of a Core in SIMULATED capture - a demonstration that recorded no media; a client says so and never "no sealed package in the evidence store"), or a code of the package itself: `PACKAGE_MISSING` (the folder is gone, e.g. quarantined), `MANIFEST_UNREADABLE`, `MANIFEST_NOT_OF_ITEM`, `CAMERA_FILE_MISSING`, `CAMERA_FILE_SIZE_MISMATCH`, `FRAGMENT_TABLE_INVALID`, `FRAGMENT_TOO_LARGE`, `SESSION_KEY_UNAVAILABLE`. An open set.

EvidenceMediaRef.description: Which media belongs to an evidence item. It names no file and no path: playback travels through the signed media session of operation 88 (E-31; the v1 MS-1 reading stays true for Simulated mode).

access.description: Core server only: what THIS caller may do with the item, so that a page view asks for nothing it would be refused (a refusal is an audited row).

play.description: This caller may open a media session for the item (operation 88): false for REAL evidence the caller does not hold (SEC35-16). A client that reads false does not ask.

readTranscript.description: This caller is inside the case scope the transcript operations (84, 86) hold for the item.

export.description: This caller has EVIDENCE_EXPORT and is inside the case scope of the item (operations 42, 87 and the download).

exports.description: Core server only, and only for a caller with `access.export`: the finished exports of the item whose archive lies in the Core's store, newest first. Each can be downloaded again through operation 87 by its `jobId`. Archives are kept until the package is removed; none is deleted by the product.

jobId.description: `EXPJ-NNNNNN`: the `{id}` of operation 87, which answers a fresh signed download path for it.

exportedBy.description: The operator ID the signed export manifest names (`export.exportedBy`).

archiveBytes.description: The length of the archive file as it lies on the Core.

archiveSha256.description: SHA-256 of the archive file, when the Core has computed it in this run; operation 87 always answers it (`archive.sha256`).

items.description: One finished export of an evidence item: the archive lies in the Core's store.

exportDestinationDefault.description: Core server only: the destination text the Core records for an export request that names none - `Case file transfer` on a Core in its own capture, `Case file transfer (simulated)` on a Core in simulated capture. A client pre-selects the destination whose recorded text equals it, so that every client offers the same default.

exportKinds.description: Core server only: the export outputs of operation 42 and whether this Core can produce each. A client offers a kind ENABLED only when its entry says `available: true`, and draws an unavailable kind disabled with its reason. Absent (Simulated mode, an older Core): only PACKAGE is offered.

available.description: True: a request of this kind is accepted. False: it is refused (`409 COMMAND_UNSUPPORTED`) before any job.

reason.description: Present exactly when `available` is false: why, as a code - `COMPOSITE_ENCODER_NOT_SELECTED` (no encoder is selected in this build).

EvidenceDetail.description: One evidence item and the reference to its media.

ok.description: True when every file, the transcript hash, the manifest and the signature verify.

at.description: When the verification ran, on the server clock.

expected.description: The sealed hash of the track.

tracks.description: One result per v1 track; a schema-v2 item answers `files` instead (C3 §3 op 41).

files.description: Schema v2: one result per camera file, both hashes and the fragment chain.

storedOk.description: Hash of the stored bytes matches the sealed value.

plainOk.description: Hash of the plaintext bytes matches the sealed value.

plainChecked.description: Present and false when the plaintext check (V-05) did not run for this file: `plainOk: false` is then "not checked", not a failed comparison. Absent: `plainOk` is the result of the check.

chainOk.description: Every fragment checkpoint continues the chain (V-11 idiom; one tampered fragment answers false — OD-02 L2).

transcriptOk.description: Schema v2: the sealed transcript hash matches the stored document; absent for an item without a transcript.

signatureOk.description: Schema v2: a real Ed25519 signature is verified with the Core public key (OD-02).

demonstration.description: Present and true on every verdict the SIMULATOR computed (a `SIMULATED` item, a v1 `DEMO_PACKAGE` item): the hashes of a demonstration record were compared and no stored media was read. A client words such a verdict as a demonstration, never as a bare "verified by the Core". Absent on the verdict of a real sealed package.

overall.description: Schema v2: PASS, or the gravest failure class among the findings.

interrupted.description: Schema v2: the package is the sealed durable prefix of an interrupted recording (V-12). A state, not a failure.

checks.description: Schema v2: the per-check report, V-01 to V-15 in order, so that a client can name the check that failed.

failureClass.description: The class of the first finding; null unless the status is FAIL.

file.description: A path inside the package, `/` separated; never a host path.

member.description: A dotted member path of the manifest.

findings.description: WHERE the check found something: names, never a value of the package.

findingCount.description: How many findings the check has when `findings` was cut; absent when it lists them all.

fragments.description: Schema v2: the fragments that did not verify, over both camera files (V-08 names the fragment). Fragments that verified are counted in `files`, not listed.

storedOk.description: The stored bytes of the fragment hash to the sealed value (V-04).

plainOk.description: The decrypted fragment hashes to the sealed value (V-05); null: not checked.

failedFragmentCount.description: Schema v2: how many fragments did not verify; larger than `fragments.length` when the list was cut.

transcriptState.description: Schema v2: what the verified package says of its transcript (seven codes; D110).

report.description: The English report line of the state; a client words the state by `code`.

transcriptModel.description: Schema v2 (decision D160): the model of the sealed transcript, from the signed manifest. For a server backend only the name exists, as reported by the STT server; version, quantisation and file hash are null and were not verified by the Core. Absent when no transcript document is sealed, for a v1 item, and when the manifest is not the signed one.

name.description: The model name the sealed manifest records.

version.description: The version the installation declared; null for a server backend.

quantisation.description: The quantisation read from the model file; null for a server backend.

modelSha256.description: SHA-256 of the model file as the Core hashed it; null for a server backend.

reportedByServer.description: True when the session's STT backend was a server: the name is what the server reported, and the Core verified nothing of the model.

report.description: The report line of the model.

sources.description: Schema v2 (V-15; R-11): the source class of every recorded source. A development package verifies with `ok: true` at the top level and `sources.code: DEVELOPMENT`; the value of the mark never changes the verdict. Absent for a v1 item: its source class is not recorded, which is never read as production.

ok.description: V-15 passed: the mark is present, well-formed and consistent. It says nothing of the value of the mark.

code.description: DEVELOPMENT: at least one source is LOCAL_DEVICE or FAKE (not a failure). DECLARED_PRODUCTION: every source reads PRODUCTION - a statement of the Core that sealed the package, not a fact the verifier proved. NOT_TRUSTWORTHY: the manifest is not the signed one or its mark is missing or inconsistent; no class is stated. UNKNOWN: no readable v2 manifest.

development.description: Recomputed by the verifier from the classes. null exactly when `code` is NOT_TRUSTWORTHY or UNKNOWN: nothing is stated, and null is never read as production.

report.description: The English source line, the first line of a verify report; a client words the state by `code`.

tracks.description: Manifest field 124 of each camera file the manifest names (one to four, D60); empty when nothing is stated.

audioIntervals.description: Manifest field 125 of each interval of the session audio track; empty when nothing is stated.

signature.description: Schema v2 (decisions D147, D178): what the verified package says of its signing KEY. A fact about the key, never the verdict: `signatureOk` passes or fails on its own merits. `developmentKey` is nullable: `null` means NOT ESTABLISHED (the package did not verify), never "not a development key". Absent for a v1 item.

developmentKey.description: True when the subject of the certificate that VERIFIED the signature carries the development-key mark (`OU=DEVELOPMENT KEY - NOT FOR PRODUCTION`); false when it does not. `null`: NOT ESTABLISHED - the manifest, the signature or the certificate did not verify (never `false` from an unverified package). A client shows "Signed with a DEVELOPMENT key - not a production signature" for true and "not established" for null.

notices.description: Schema v2 (decision D178): what the package format does NOT cover. Named statements that fail nothing; a client shows each one and never collapses it. Absent for a v1 item.

code.description: `AUDIT_EXTRACT_NOT_SIGNED` (every v2 result): `audit-session-extract.jsonl` is in the package and its content is covered by no hash and no signature. `EXPORT_FOLDER_UNEXPECTED_FILE` (only when there is such a file): the `export/` folder of the package holds a file that is no finished export - a `.partial` a stopped export left, a name no export writes, or anything in a sub-folder; the sealed set is not affected. `REVISION_APPEND_PENDING` (only while there is such a file): a transcript revision is being written - `transcript/transcript-revisions.json.next` lies in the package; it fails nothing; verify again shortly. `SIGNED_BY_COMPROMISED_KEY` (only for a package under such a key): the manifest or a transcript revision is signed by a key that was later MARKED COMPROMISED, so the signature alone proves nothing any more. **This notice is not "fails nothing"**: it stands beside a verdict that took the mark into account and its `report` says which - the answer is a pass ONLY when the package is the one this Core recorded when it sealed the item (its manifest digest and the head of its revisions equal what the Core stored), and a failure otherwise. An answer with this code is never a plain pass: a client shows it as a state of the signing key, not among what the signature does not cover. `HOST_PROFILE_NOT_ASKED` (only for a package whose manifest carries the member `hostProfileNotAsked`): the package was sealed by a production Core on a platform where the checks of the host profile are not run; it fails nothing and changes no verdict. `VIDEO_ABSENT_IN_SESSION` (only for a package whose manifest carries the member `absentInSession` on a track): a camera stopped delivering pictures inside the session; the line states per track how often, the two measured bounds of the time in ms, and whether the last absence ended; it fails nothing and changes no verdict. `AUDIO_ABSENT_ON_RESTART` (only for a package whose manifest carries the member `audio.absentOnRestart`): the capture was restarted inside the session and no sound was recorded across the restart; the line states how often and the two measured bounds of the time in ms; it fails nothing and changes no verdict. `AUDIO_SAMPLES_NOT_RECEIVED` (only for a package whose manifest carries the member `audio.samplesNotReceived`): the audio was captured on a path that does not deliver every sample (bench capture path of a Mac); the line states, in whole samples of the highest capture attempt, how many samples of the track arrived, how many are silence the recorder inserted, and the runs of 100 ms or more (listed, not listed, the longest) - or that the amount was measured up to a sample only, or not measured; sound that did not arrive is not in the recording, and the places of the inserted silence are not the places of the missing sound; it fails nothing and changes no verdict - a package can be untouched and its audio incomplete. `AUDIO_ONE_CAPTURE_GROUP` (only beside the previous one, when two of its records state the same capture group): PRIMARY and STANDBY were channels of one device recorded by one capture program, so a switch between them was not a switch to an independent source; it fails nothing and changes no verdict.

report.description: The report line of the notice.

EvidenceVerifyResult.description: The verdict of record of an integrity verification (schema v2: per-file chains, transcript hash, real signature).

DeviceInventory.description: The devices of the Core: eight slices of the Core state, each in its wire form (schema v2 adds `captureConfig`).

cameraId.description: The camera the monitor shows: one of the four video tracks (D60, 2026-11-04).

channel.description: The audio channel whose CLIP latch is reset: `AUDIO-01`..`AUDIO-04` (D61, 2026-11-04: four simultaneous channels).

confirm.description: Must be `true` to cycle the PoE port of a camera (OD-22); ignored for other devices.

RestartDeviceRequest.description: Optional request body of `POST /api/v1/device/{id}/restart` (schema v2: the PoE-cycle confirmation).

StorageDetail.description: The storage of the Core and its retention policy: two slices of the Core state, each in its wire form.

retentionPolicy.description: The retention policy. Sent without `retentionDays`, it sets the days of that policy: 30, 90, 365 or 3,650.

retentionDays.description: Days an item is kept before it may be archived: a whole number from 1 to 3,650.

autoArchive.description: Whether an item is archived by itself when its retention ends.

StoragePolicyRequest.description: Request body of `POST /api/v1/storage/policy`: the members to change. A member that is left out keeps its value.

NetworkStatus.description: The network of the Core and the link of the tablet: two slices of the Core state, each in its wire form.

cameraOffsets.description: Schema v2: camera clock offsets via telemetry; absent while no camera has reported one.

deviceId.description: The camera device, e.g. CAM-01.

offsetMs.description: The camera clock minus the Core clock, as the telemetry reported it.

source.description: How it was measured (open code, e.g. NTP_ONVIF, RTCP_TELEMETRY).

TimeStatus.description: The time service of the Core device and, from schema v2, the camera clock offsets.

auditHead.description: Hash of the newest audit row of the stored chain; 64 zeros when the chain is empty.

auditTotal.description: Rows of the stored chain: the `seq` of its newest row.

evidenceVerification.description: Core server only: how many sealed items have / have no verification of record, counted over the whole evidence list by each item's `verification.status`. `passed + failed + neverVerified = sealed`. Absent: not stated (Simulated mode, an older Core).

sealed.description: Items that are sealed (`sealedAt` set). Never-sealed records are not counted.

passed.description: Sealed items whose verification of record is PASS.

failed.description: Sealed items whose verification of record is FAIL.

neverVerified.description: Sealed items with no verification of record (NOT_RUN).

SecurityStatus.description: The `security` slice in its wire form, with the head and the row count of the audit chain.

type.description: Only rows of this audit type.

actorId.description: Only rows whose actor is this operator (`OPR-NNN`).

evidenceId.description: Only rows of this evidence item.

order.description: By `seq`: ASC is the order of the chain, oldest first, and is used when omitted; DESC is newest first.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

AuditListQuery.description: Query of `GET /api/v1/audit`: filters, the order and the paging members of API-9.

rows.description: Audit rows in the order asked for, each with its full hashed body.

head.description: Hash of the newest row of the stored chain at the time of the read.

total.description: Rows of the stored chain at the time of the read, whatever the filters.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

AuditPage.description: One page of audit rows. Rows are ordered by `seq`, so paging stays stable while rows are appended.

checked.description: Rows checked: every row of the view.
Rows that verified before the first bad one.

index.description: Position of the first bad row in the view (`audit.rows`).

ChainVerifyResult.description: Result of the shared chain check over the audit view: the simulator's `ChainVerifyResult`.

epoch.description: The epoch the discarded chain ended in.

head.description: Head hash of the discarded chain.

resetAt.description: When the reset ran, on the server clock.

actorId.description: The operator who ran it; null for a reset from the command line.

scenario.description: The scenario the reset loaded (`idle` for a reset to the seed state).

AuditChainLineageEntry.description: One audit chain that a demo reset or a scenario load discarded.

view.description: The shared check over the audit view the engine holds: what the screens show, and what the demo fault AUDIT_TAMPER breaks.

checked.description: The `seq` the stored chain has been verified through.

head.description: Head hash of the stored chain.

firstBadSeq.description: `seq` of the first stored row that does not verify; null while the chain verifies.

stored.description: The check over the stored table, which no demo fault can break. It is incremental: a call verifies only the rows above the last verified one.

lineage.description: The chains that earlier resets discarded, newest first, at most 20.

lineageTotal.description: How many chains were discarded in all.

AuditChainStatus.description: Status of the audit chain: the view, the stored table, and the lineage of discarded chains.

reason.description: Purpose of the export: 5 to 500 characters after trimming. It is recorded in the AUDIT_EXPORTED row.

destination.description: Destination or approved media identifier: at most 120 UTF-16 code units after trimming. Omitted or empty means "Audit archive (simulated)".

rows.description: Stored audit rows the export covers: every row before the AUDIT_EXPORTED row it wrote.

head.description: Hash of the last of those rows: the `prevHash` of the AUDIT_EXPORTED row.

AuditExportAccepted.description: Export accepted. The ExportEvent is the AUDIT_EXPORTED audit row it wrote; the client builds the file.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

EventListQuery.description: Query of `GET /api/v1/events`: filters and the paging members of API-9.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

EventPage.description: One page of operational events. Events are ordered by `seq`, so paging stays stable while events are appended.

components.description: Core server only: the versions of the components of THIS Core, each defined in one place. They are the only version statements about the real system: `device.softwareVersion`, `device.identity.coreSoftwareVersion`, `device.identity.tabletAppVersion` and the versions of the `update` slice are values of the hosted demonstration model and are never shown as the version of a Core in its own capture. The web console and the mobile app each state their OWN build version; the app version of a paired device is `appVersion` of the paired-devices list. Absent: Simulated mode, or an older Core.

name.description: The service name of the Core, as operation 1 states it (`service`).

version.description: The version of the Core server: the value operation 1 answers as `version` and a sealed manifest states as `device.softwareVersion`.

captureWorker.description: The capture worker. Present on a Core in its own capture; absent on a Core in SIMULATED capture, which starts none.

version.description: The release word of the capture worker this Core starts, `capture-worker/<major>.<minor>.<patch>`: the one version it accepts at the handshake.
The version of the API contract document this Core serves (`info.version` of its OpenAPI document).

SystemStatus.description: The system page of the Core: five slices of the Core state, each in its wire form, and the versions of its components.

runId.description: ID of the run, `DIAG-NNNNNN`. Its checks resolve in the `diagnostics` slice.

DiagnosticsRunStarted.description: A diagnostics run was started, or one is still in progress.

restarted.description: How many Core services were restarted: every one that was not stopped.

ServicesRestarted.description: Result of a restart of the Core services.

SettingsUpdateRequest.description: Request body of `POST /api/v1/settings`: the display preferences to change. A member that is left out keeps its value.

AlertList.description: The alerts of the Core: one slice of the Core state in its wire form, under its slice name.

deviceId.description: A capture device of the registry, e.g. `CAM-01` (`dbc-3 §B.2`).

profile.description: Media profile code (open set, OD-06/OD-07); absent: the device default.

CaptureConfigCameraUpdate.description: One camera line of `CaptureConfigUpdate`: which capture device feeds which video track.

inputId.description: A mic input of the selector, `MIC-NN`.

deviceId.description: A capture device of the registry, e.g. `MIC-01`.

transport.description: Transport code (open set, e.g. `POE`, `USB`, `ANALOG`); absent: the device default.

channel.description: BY CHANNEL (D133 (1) generalized by D61, 2026-11-04: a channel is assignable alone): when every line carries `channel`, each line puts its input on the slot of its channel - one to four lines, no channel twice, each with `deviceId` equal to `inputId`, any registered `MIC-NN`; the slot of a channel the body does not name keeps what it holds, and the named channels are the replacing set. Absent on every line: the line edits the input it names (the earlier form).

CaptureConfigMicUpdate.description: One mic line of `CaptureConfigUpdate`: which capture device stands behind which input; with `channel`, the input that takes the slot of that channel (D61: four numbered channels).

unassign.description: The selector slots this body clears: a video track (`VIDEO-01`..`VIDEO-04`) or a microphone channel (`MIC-01`..`MIC-04`; D61, 2026-11-04: the roles became the numbered channels), each at most once. A cleared slot has no line in the answer. A slot that the same body assigns (the `trackId` of a camera line, the `channel` of a mic line) is `422 INVALID_INPUT`. Clearing a slot that is already empty changes nothing and writes no audit row.

CaptureConfigUpdateRequest.description: Request body of `POST /api/v1/capture/config` (C3 §2.3 op 78): a partial `{ cameras?[], mics?[], unassign?[] }`.

trackId.description: The video track this camera becomes the source of.

username.description: Camera credential username: 1 to 120 printable ASCII characters without `<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'` and backslash. Write-only: never returned, logged or audited (RK-12).

secret.description: Camera credential secret: 1 to 1024 printable ASCII characters, taken exactly as sent (never trimmed). Write-only: never returned, logged or audited (RK-12; C-N8).

CaptureCredentialWriteRequest.description: Request body of `POST /api/v1/capture/devices/{id}/credential` (C3 §2.3 op 89). A write-only pair: the value never comes back on any path.

inputId.description: The mic input to move behind AUDIO-01, `MIC-NN`: one of the two inputs of the transcription pair (channels `MIC-01` and `MIC-02`; D61, 2026-11-04: the other returns to channel 2 — the other two channels record untouched).

reason.description: Why the operator switched; audited as text, never as a secret.

switchedAt.description: Core instant the switch took effect (never the client clock, E-13).

intervalFromMs.description: Media-pts start of the interval the switch opened.

AudioSourceState.description: The active/standby pair after a switch (`C3 §2.3` op 81); mirrors the session slice member.

seq.description: Interval number within the session, from 1: the manifest's rule (ev §B.5) and the table's (`session_audio_intervals_seq_check`). Pass D6: the text said "from 0"; no Core ever answered 0 in real capture.

inputId.description: The mic device of this interval, `MIC-NN`.

toMs.description: Media-pts end (ms); null while the interval is open.

toAt.description: UTC-ms record of the end; null while open.

switchedBy.description: The operator of the manual toggle that opened it; null when the run opened it.

reason.description: What opened the interval (OD-09/OD-11: every switch is operator-initiated).

AudioSourceIntervalEntry.description: One interval of one mic input inside AUDIO-01 (`session_audio_intervals`, `dbc-3 §B.5`).

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

AudioSourceIntervalPage.description: One page of audio-source intervals (op 82; API-9).

state.description: The session state while sealing (FINALIZING, or SEALED/RECOVERY around it).

progressPct.description: Whole-percent progress over the v2 steps, forward-only (E-13).

etaMs.description: Estimated milliseconds left; null before the estimate holds.

resumed.description: True when this seal is a RECOVERY resume from a checkpoint (MB-06; OD-08). On a Core in real capture: a START of the Core ran the seal again - never an automatic retry of the same process, never the on-demand retry of operation 33.

updatedAt.description: Core instant of the last recompute.

SealingProgress.description: Sealing progress v2 (`C3 §2.3` op 83); mirrors the session `finalization` slice with the v2 steps.

text.description: The spoken text; API-13 text rule.

speaker.description: Speaker label when diarization labelled it; null when UNAVAILABLE (D226 labels part; never blocks text).

insertedSilenceMs.description: THE MARK ON THE SEGMENT (Core server only; task 4 row N2): this many whole milliseconds of the segment (`startMs` to `endMs`) are SILENCE THE RECORDER INSERTED, in runs of 100 ms or more that the signed manifest of the item lists with their positions (`audio.samplesNotReceived[].insertedRuns`). No audio arrived from the microphone in that time; the text of the segment is the engine's and is not cut - the segment is marked, not split. A client shows the mark at the segment and never joins two segments into one line or paragraph across a listed run. ABSENT: no listed run overlaps the segment - never to be read as "this segment holds every word that was spoken".

documentVersion.description: Canonical document version; the VALUE is owned by transcript-spec §0.2 (TRANSCRIPT_DOC_VERSION) — cited, not duplicated (J.9).

language.description: Transcript language (D226; fixed for this phase).

sha256.description: Hash of this canonical document as stored.

machineTranscriptHash.description: Hash of the SEALED machine transcript; revisions never change it (OD-15).

revision.description: Current max(revision_no); 0 when no revision exists (SEC35-21).

audioNotSampleContinuous.description: THE STATEMENT AT THE HEAD OF THE TRANSCRIPT (Core server only; task 4 row N2; decisions U25 (3), C110 (2)): the audio this text was made from is NOT SAMPLE-CONTINUOUS - it was captured on a path that does not deliver every sample (bench capture path of a Mac). Sound that did not arrive is not in the recording. Silence of the same total length was inserted by the recorder; its places are not the places of the missing sound. The numbers are whole samples of the highest capture attempt, the ones of the verify notice `AUDIO_SAMPLES_NOT_RECEIVED`, read from the SIGNED manifest of the item. A client shows this statement with its numbers at the head of the transcript and never collapses it; a transcript of such audio does not hold every word that was spoken. ABSENT: the manifest of the item states no measured shortfall - never to be read as "the audio is complete".

arrivedSamples.description: Samples of the track that arrived (`trackSamples` less `insertedSamples`); null when the amount was not measured.

trackSamples.description: Samples the session's own clock expected up to the recorder's last account: the length of the track when that account closed it. null when the amount was not measured.

insertedSamples.description: Samples of the track that are silence the recorder inserted, not sound; null when the amount was not measured.

listedRuns.description: Runs of inserted silence of 100 ms or more that the signed manifest lists with their positions; the segments they overlap carry `insertedSilenceMs`.

runsNotListed.description: Runs of 100 ms or more that the manifest counts and does NOT list: they have no position and mark no segment.

TranscriptDocument.description: The machine transcript of an evidence item (op 84).

baseRevision.description: The item's CURRENT max(revision_no) as the caller saw it (0 when none). A mismatch answers 409 TRANSCRIPT_REVISION_CONFLICT; the check runs inside the minting transaction (SEC35-21; dbc-3 §B.9).

segmentIndex.description: Which segment of the machine transcript to correct.

from.description: The text being replaced. It MUST be the CURRENT text of the segment: the `to` of the newest revision that changed the segment, else the sealed text. Anything else answers `422 INVALID_INPUT` with `details.reason: REVISION_FROM_NOT_CURRENT_TEXT`; nothing is signed and nothing is appended (ruling D221 (2)).

note.description: REQUIRED (pass D6): why the revision was made, 5 to 500 characters after trimming. It is stored as the revision's `reason` (dbc-3 §B.9: NOT NULL, 5..500), is inside the signed revision body, and travels to the audit row as `reason`. A revision of evidence without a stated reason is refused: 422 INVALID_INPUT.

number.description: The 1-based revision number (max+1 inside the minting transaction).

authorId.description: Who revised (OD-15: author recorded; no approval flow).

baseRevision.description: The max(revision_no) this revision was built on (SEC35-21).

machineTranscriptHash.description: The sealed machine transcript this revision binds to — byte-unchanged by it (OD-15).

signedBy.description: Id of the Core key that signed (OD-15: Core key signs; never the key itself).

signature.description: Signature over the revision (dbc-3 §B.9/§C.4 pairs; SEC35-20 certificate is server-side).

reason.description: Why the revision was made: the note its author gave, as stored and as signed with the revision (op 85 `note`). Absent only where the stored revision holds none. Never a default.

TranscriptRevision.description: One signed transcript revision (append-only; V-11 walks the parent_sha256 chain).

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

TranscriptRevisionPage.description: One page of transcript revisions (op 86; API-9).

jobId.description: `EXPJ-NNNNNN`: `EXPJ-` and the six digits of the export ID of operation 42 (`EXP-000012` -> `EXPJ-000012`).

derived.description: True for a COMPOSITE output: marked derived and hashed in the export manifest (OD-16).

archive.description: Core server only, on a COMPLETE job whose archive lies in the Core's store (wave H C1; ruling D200): the length and SHA-256 of the archive FILE. The archive carries its export manifest and signature inside and therefore cannot contain its own hash: this answer and the download's audit row are where it is stated. `npm run evidence:verify-export -- <archive> --sha256 <this value>` holds a received file to it.

failureReason.description: SCREAMING_SNAKE cause when FAILED; the EVIDENCE_EXPORT_FAILED row carries the same code. An open set of codes. Among them: `COMPOSITE_ENCODER_NOT_SELECTED` (a COMPOSITE was asked for and no encoder is selected), `EXPORT_INTERRUPTED` (the server stopped while the job ran; the job is not resumed - ask again), `SESSION_KEY_UNAVAILABLE`, `SOURCE_VERIFY_FAILED`, `SOURCE_SIGNED_BY_COMPROMISED_KEY` (the package rests on a signing key marked compromised and is not the one the Core recorded at the seal; a package under such a key that IS the one of record is exported, and its export manifest states the mark in `sourceSigningKey`), `PLAINTEXT_HASH_MISMATCH`, `EXPORT_WRITE_FAILED`, `EXPORT_FAILED`.

download.description: Core server only, and only on a COMPLETE job of an item whose sealed package lies in the Core's store: a short-lived signed path that serves the finished archive as an attachment (ruling D178). Bound to the caller's operator and sign-in session and to this export; the request needs EVIDENCE_EXPORT and, for REAL evidence, the case scope of SEC35-16. Each download is audited. Absent in Simulated mode and for a simulated export.

path.description: Same-origin path of the registry-external `GET /exports/<token>`. A BEARER value: never logged, never audited, never stored, never a cache key.

expiresAt.description: Core instant the path dies (`EVIDENCE_MEDIA_SESSION_TTL_MS` after this answer). Poll again for a fresh one.

EvidenceExportJob.description: The background export job of op 42/87 (NM-12; OD-16).

fileId.description: The camera file to play (D60: one of the four tracks; a legacy package offers its own two); absent: `VIDEO-01`.

seekIndex.description: Fix wave K Z1 (ruling D224 (1)): asks for the INDEXED VIEW of the file - the same decrypted bytes plus ONE segment index (`sidx`) built from the signed manifest fragment table, for a player that cannot seek a fragmented file without one. Absent: the stream as before. The answer states whether the session serves it.

EvidenceMediaSessionRequest.description: Optional request body of `POST /api/v1/evidence/{id}/media-sessions` (op 88): the camera file of the session.

fileId.description: Which camera file this session plays (D60, 2026-11-04: the package's own list, up to four).

url.description: Signed loopback URL with the mts_ token (SEC35-13). Bearer value: never logged, never audited, never replicated (E-31).

expiresAt.description: Core instant the URL dies; the replay window is exactly this TTL (SEC35-12).

ranges.description: The route answers Range requests (NM-11 playback).

seekIndex.description: Fix wave K Z1 (ruling D224 (1)): present, always `true`, exactly when the URL of THIS session serves the INDEXED VIEW of the file (the request asked `seekIndex: true` and the signed fragment table yields an exact index): the same decrypted bytes plus one segment index between the init segment and the first fragment; lengths and Range offsets of the URL are those of the view. Absent: the stream as sealed - a player that needs an index cannot seek it. Nothing of the sealed package, the export or Verify differs.

EvidenceMediaSession.description: A short-lived signed evidence-media session (op 88; live-only — Simulated mode plays the bundled demo media instead).

reachable.description: The backend answered the last test.

modelAvailable.description: The configured model was available at the last test.

testedAt.description: When the last test ran, epoch milliseconds on the Core clock.

SttLastTest.description: The outcome of the last `testSttConnection` call. No speed figure is ever recorded (D230).

enabled.description: False: no transcriber work in the next session; the package records `transcript.state = DISABLED`.

backend.description: `omlx-server` (development on this Mac) or `cpu-local` (whisper.cpp on the Core).

endpoint.description: The loopback endpoint of the server backend (OD-13). Absent when none is stored.

model.description: Model id (server backend) or model reference (`cpu-local`). Never a secret.

credentialSet.description: True when a credential is configured. The credential itself is never returned.

credentialKind.description: How the credential is held; absent when none is set. A flag, never a value.

revision.description: Optimistic revision: send it back in `updateSttConfig`.

updatedBy.description: The operator of the last change; absent for the seeded configuration.

updatedAt.description: When the configuration last changed, epoch milliseconds.
